studies.label: Online triad experiment: individual-group-individual AGI movie-plot task
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Triads were randomized. The condition-level Kruskal-Wallis tests do not report adjustment for triad clustering. The separate, excluded OLS models used heteroscedasticity-robust HC3 standard errors after group random-intercept models were abandoned; a group-clustered robustness check was described as substantively identical, without numerical creativity standard errors. PDF p. 13, Section 3.9. No uncertainty is printed for any pairwise creativity contrast.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract, Methods (n_randomized); PDF p. 7, Section 3.1 (clusters_per_arm); PDF p. 18, Section 4.3 (n_analyzed refers to human speakers in the discourse clustering analysis, not a printed creativity-analysis count).
counts_source.quote: 224 university students were randomly assigned [...] Human-only Control condition (30 groups) [...] Supportive-AI condition (33 groups) [...] Contrarian-AI condition (34 groups) [...] Across all clusters, 291 speakers were identified (224 human, 67 AI).

arms.name: Human-only Control
arms.description: Human-only collaborative triads; a human teammate occupies the position filled by AI in the other conditions. PDF p. 7, Section 3.1. Coded other_aid because human partners are the active comparison.

arms.name: Supportive-AI
arms.description: Human participants collaborate with an undisclosed, supportive AI teammate that affirms contributions, invites input, and builds consensus. PDF pp. 7 and 9, Sections 3.1 and 3.3; Appendix B, PDF pp. 29-30.

arms.name: Contrarian-AI
arms.description: Human participants collaborate with an undisclosed, contrarian AI teammate that challenges suggestions and interrupts consensus. PDF pp. 7 and 9, Sections 3.1 and 3.3; Appendix B, PDF pp. 28-29.

studies.task: University students recruited via Prolific wrote an individual AGI movie-plot synopsis, discussed a shared story outline in a triad, and then wrote a revised individual synopsis without access to baseline writing or group-chat logs (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2; Appendix A, PDF p. 28).

ai_tool.name: GPT-5-based generative models
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.3: AI collaborators were implemented using GPT-5-based generative models configured to emulate human conversational behaviour. The exact model identifier and release year are not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration statement or registration link was identified in the complete manuscript, including Appendices A-B.

estimates.outcome: Creative performance change: Divergent Semantic Integration (pre-post change)
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) measures semantic expansiveness and associative breadth within each individual synopsis. Pre/post DSI scores were standardized and differenced to obtain a creativity change score. The embedding model, standardization reference, and score distribution are not printed. This is an automated score of individual writing, not similarity across people.

sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 (outcome definition; Table 2 also identifies this as creative performance)
sources.quote: Each participant produced a 50-100 word movie plot synopsis both before and after collaboration; DSI scores were standardised and differenced to obtain a creativity change score.

sources.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 3.2 (individual post-task writing after collaboration; see also Figure 2)
sources.quote: Following the discussion, participants completed a second individual post-task writing activity to produce a revised plot synopsis (without having access to their baseline task writing and group chat logs)

sources.locator: PDF p. 18, Section 4.4, first paragraph (omnibus finding only; not a pairwise p-value)
sources.quote: Kruskal-Wallis omnibus tests indicated that condition did not significantly affect intrinsic cognitive load, germane cognitive load, or creative performance gains (all p > .05).

estimates.notes: Comparison retained from the screening map with all numerical contrast fields null. The paper describes creative gains as stable across conditions but prints only a Kruskal-Wallis omnibus bound, all p > .05, across all experimental conditions. It reports no pairwise creativity test, arm means, SDs, SEs, confidence intervals, condition coefficients, or effect sizes. The omnibus bound is not assigned to this pairwise p_value. Creativity-analysis human counts are not printed; the overall discourse-analysis count is not imputed here, and arm counts are not computed from triad composition. The OLS creativity model is excluded because it adjusts for agency profiles measured during treatment and reports only whole-model statistics. The post-task synopsis was written after the AI-assisted chat without access to chat logs, supporting immediate after_ai. Baseline/post measurement is not a randomized within-person condition order.

not_extracted.what: Emergent agency profiles, profile-specific code proportions, and human/AI speaker distributions
not_extracted.reason: Unsupervised profiles describe discourse behavior; profile membership was not randomized and is not a creative-output outcome. The analysis also includes AI speakers. PDF pp. 12-13, Section 3.8; PDF pp. 17-19, Section 4.3 and Figures 8-9.

not_extracted.what: Creative performance change: OLS model adjusted for emergent agency profile
not_extracted.reason: Excluded under the rule against adjustment for variables measured after treatment: agency profiles were derived from utterances during the manipulated group discussion. PDF p. 13, Section 3.9, specifies Q(Outcome) ∼C(cluster) + C(condition). PDF p. 19, Section 4.4, reports: "Finally, creative performance gains, as measured by changes in Divergent Semantic Integration, were not predicted by either cluster or condition (F = 1.20, p = .310, R2 = .029)." These are full-model statistics, not any pairwise treatment effect. Neither condition coefficients nor numerical group-clustered standard errors are printed.

The outline was produced during the AI-available discussion, but no creativity score or between-condition output-quality contrast is reported for it. The scored output was the individual pre/post synopsis. PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2; PDF p. 10, Section 3.5 and Table 2.

not_extracted.what: Separate pilot study of perceived AI human-likeness
not_extracted.reason: The pilot assessed perceptions of the AI teammate, not creative output, and does not contribute people to the main randomized experiment. PDF p. 9, Section 3.3.
Detection of the AI teammate is a perception/manipulation check, not creativity or diversity scored on participant output. PDF p. 9, Section 3.3.

open_items: The creativity analyses do not print total or per-arm human Ns or exclusions. The study-level n_analyzed is the printed count of human speakers in the discourse clustering analysis and must not be used as the creativity-analysis N (PDF pp. 13 and 18-19). Per-arm person counts are not derived from group composition.

No pairwise DSI-change means, SDs, mean differences, SEs, confidence intervals, standardized effects, or exact pairwise p-values are printed. The unadjusted omnibus result supplies only a bound and no creativity-specific H statistic, degrees of freedom, or epsilon-squared (PDF p. 18, Section 4.4).

No numerical uncertainty accounting for randomized triads is available for an eligible creativity contrast. The group-clustered robustness statement refers to models adjusted for post-treatment agency profiles (PDF p. 13, Section 3.9).
The DSI embedding model and the reference used to standardize pre/post scores are not specified (PDF p. 10, Section 3.5).
The GPT-5-based tool is named, but its precise model identifier and release year are not printed (PDF p. 9, Section 3.3); year is null.
Whether a separate supplement exists is not established. Internal appendices contain task instructions and persona prompts, not additional creative-performance statistics (PDF pp. 28-30).

No public data or code URL is provided. The Data Availability statement says data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request and are not public due to privacy or ethical restrictions (PDF p. 23).
notes: The full markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks, including references and Appendices A-B. All tables, figures, and internal appendices were inspected, and cited passages and recorded counts were checked with pymupdf against the PDF. PDF page numbers match printed page numbers. The complete creativity-statistic inventory consists of the unadjusted Kruskal-Wallis omnibus bound in the estimate source quotations and the full-model OLS F, p, and R2 values preserved in not_extracted. No additional output-scored creativity statistic is printed or recoverable from a figure. The three estimate records preserve the screening comparisons with null numerical fields; they are not three reported pairwise effects. Sources with empty fields support the outcome, timing, and omnibus narrative without assigning omnibus statistics to pairwise fields. No numeric contrast, standardized effect, person count, or uncertainty was calculated. No shared sample or preregistration is stated. Review of the manuscript and extraction was completed by extractor B on 2026-10-10; subsequent verification and reconciliation are pending.
